relations.note: Xochipilli and Cinteotl merge or overlap as flowering, maize, and youthful-solar powers.
Cinteotl is named within the hymn’s flower, maize, music, and solar imagery.
Ixtlilton appears beside the Xochipilli-Cinteotl figure in the ballcourt scene.
Sahagún explicitly states that Macuilxochitl was also called Xochipilli.
Macuilcuetzpalin and Macuilxochitl appear together among the male pleasure and excess gods.
Macuilcozcacuauhtli and Macuilxochitl appear together among the male pleasure and excess gods.
Macuiltochtli and Macuilxochitl appear together among the male pleasure and excess gods.
Macuilmalinalli and Macuilxochitl appear together among the male pleasure and excess gods.
The female dead are juxtaposed with Macuilxochitl’s male pleasure-god series.
Quetzalcoatl appears opposite the Xochipilli-Cinteotl side; the scene’s meaning remains disputed.
A Cihuacoatl or Coatlicue-type goddess appears opposite Xochipilli; her precise identification is disputed.
